A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PointMapPolicy and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices A–E. The added material can be reliably distinguished from retained and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoboCasa and CALVIN evaluations, six real-robot experiments, and ablation and activation-map analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a controlled comparison of point-cloud encoders on RoboCasa.

M1.justification: The point-map construction, modality fusion, xLSTM backbone, diffusion objective, and four-step DDIM inference remain unchanged. The added encoder variants are experimental comparators, not changes to PMP.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 RoboCasa tasks, CALVIN ABC-to-D setting, and six real-robot tasks. The new encoder comparison reuses existing RoboCasa coverage without adding a task or test scenario.

E2.justification: New Section 4.2 evaluates PointNet-xyz, PointNet-color, PointPatch, and 3D-Lifting against PMP-xyz with a shared X-Block backbone. This substantially expands encoder-level comparisons; the original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled evaluation design across the 16 RoboCasa tasks, holding the xLSTM policy backbone fixed while varying point-cloud encoding. It specifies 1024-point sampling for PointNet variants and 256 patches of 32 points for PointPatch. Existing benchmark splits, budgets, metrics, and checkpoint-selection procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and new Figure 5 add a substantial ablation addressing whether advantages over other 3D policies arise from encoding rather than backbone differences. The existing fusion, vision-encoder, and appendix activation-map analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing three-seed information and uncertainty reporting are retained. The new encoder plot introduces no additional run-count information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 adds per-task and average results showing PMP-xyz outperforming four alternative encoders under the shared-backbone protocol. Its 49.12% average is retained from v1, not a new performance gain. Tables 1–3, latency results, and earlier analysis figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) and the mathematical construction remain unchanged. Section 3.3 adds indexed pixel-to-point correspondence notation that restates the image-aligned XYZ grid already described in v1; it introduces no substantive new assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the claimed ablation contribution to include point-cloud processing methods, with a corresponding new research question. The abstract and conclusion retain the original novelty, performance, and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies backbone differences as a confound and interprets the new ablation as evidence that point-map encoding drives improvements. It additionally claims independence from downstream policy architecture, although only one backbone is controlled. Existing modality interpretations and Section 6 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new comparators' sampling, patch construction, pooling, transformer processing, and frozen CLIP features. It removes the promise to release source code upon publication, while retaining the project-page link and existing hyperparameter and hardware appendices; an actual code-availability change is not established.

R1.justification: The introduction expands its positioning against downsampling and feature-lifting approaches, emphasizing geometric-information loss and spatial-structure preservation. All 60 referenced works are retained; citation reordering does not introduce new works.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory motivation and point-map explanation, inserts a Point Cloud Encoding subsection and research question, and adds acknowledgments. The remaining narrative and appendix structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the encoder-comparison line plot as Figure 5. The previous ablation plot becomes Figure 6, later figures are renumbered, and some displays move. Existing figure content and table designs are retained without extensive redesign.

improvement.justification: The controlled encoder comparison in Section 4.2 strengthens attribution of RoboCasa gains to point-map encoding by addressing backbone differences in v1's comparisons. Added encoder recipes and pixel correspondence explanations improve clarity. The gain is limited by testing only one backbone despite claiming architecture independence, and by removing the code-release commitment. Overall, the added control provides a useful net improvement in evidential support.
